title: Quadratic completed equation at a rational geometric node
statement: Let $F$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $F$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], of topological Krull dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $z\in X$ be a closed point [def-weil-closed-points] which is $F$-rational, meaning that the structure map $F\to\kappa(z)$ to its residue field [def-weil-residue-field] is an isomorphism. Let $\overline F/F$ be an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $\bar z$ be the $\overline F$-rational point of $X_{\overline F}$ [def-pc-base-change] induced by $z$. Suppose $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X_{\overline F},\bar z}$ is isomorphic as a ring to $\overline F[[u,v]]/(uv)$. Then there are $a,b,c\in F$ with $b^2-4ac\ne0$ and an $F$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,z}\cong F[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$. Completions are maximal-ideal-adic [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and the power series rings are [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].

source.place: Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal), implication (3) to (2), followed by Tag 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), condition (3), with residue field equal to the ground field.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}S\ni z$; by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] $S$ is a finitely generated $F$-algebra. The rational point gives $\epsilon:S\to F$. Put $K=\overline F$, $\mathfrak p=\ker\epsilon$, $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$, $R=S\otimes_FK$, $\mathfrak q=\ker(\epsilon\otimes_FK:R\to K)$, $B=R_{\mathfrak q}$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qB$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $U\times_F\operatorname{Spec}K=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is open in $X_K$, and $\bar z$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $\epsilon\otimes_FK$, i.e. the point $\mathfrak q$; so [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] gives $A=\mathcal O_{X,z}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{X_K,\bar z}$. $R$ is finitely generated over $K$ with $R/\mathfrak q=K$ via the structure map, and by hypothesis $\widehat B\cong K[[u,v]]/(uv)$ as rings. So [lem-trf-geometric-node-fitting-depth] applies to $K,R,\mathfrak q$: $J_B=\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega_{R/K})B=\mathfrak n$ and $\operatorname{depth}B=1$.

source.place: Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal), algebraically closed case: equivalence of (3) with (5) via Tag 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-geometric-fitting-depth-descent] with $k=F$, $\Omega=K$, the algebra $S$, the maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ and the prime $\mathfrak q$ of step 1. Its inverse image in $S$ is $\mathfrak p$: $s\otimes1\in\mathfrak q$ iff $\epsilon(s)=0$. Its $B$, $\mathfrak n$ and $J_B$ are those of step 1, so its hypotheses $J_B=\mathfrak n$ and $\operatorname{depth}B=1$ hold. It gives $J_A:=\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega_{S/F})A=\mathfrak m$ and $\operatorname{depth}\widehat A=1$ (its separability conclusion is trivial here, $S/\mathfrak p=F$).

source.place: Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal), arbitrary-field paragraphs: Fitting ideal commutes with field extension, flat descent of depth (algebra.tex Tag 0337, lemma-apply-grothendieck).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-separable-closed-point-formal-presentation] to $S$ at $\mathfrak p$ with $k=F$ ($F/F$ is finite separable): $\widehat A$ is Noetherian local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\widehat A$ and residue field $F$; its $F$-algebra section $\sigma:F\to\widehat A$ is the structural map, being $F$-linear on $F$; and $\widehat A=F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]/(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$, $n\ge2$, kernel in $(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$, with Jacobian cokernel $\Omega_{A/F}\otimes_A\widehat A\cong\Omega_{S/F}\otimes_S\widehat A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization]. By clauses (1),(2) of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] the $(n-1)$-minor ideal is $\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega_{S/F})\widehat A=J_A\widehat A=\mathfrak m\widehat A$ (step 2): every kernel row is a linear combination of the relation rows, so multilinear expansion equates the two minor ideals.

source.place: Tags 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), condition (3) to (1), and 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), condition (3); the rational-residue-field instance of 0C4D (3) to (2).

proof.text: The depth from step 2 and the minor ideal from step 3 give condition (a) of [lem-trf-formal-jacobian-quadratic-criterion]. Its implication (a) to (b) gives $a,b,c\in F$, $b^2-4ac\ne0$, and the required complete local $F$-algebra isomorphism. Its $F$-structure is the original one by the coefficient-section check in step 3.
